keyFindings.text: Drift is already detectable without a new mechanism: per-row `vec_content_hash` catches text drift at refresh, and `readAdvisorEmbeddingStaleness` compares the active embedder pointer's model and dimension against the stored vector summary and returns `stale` with a reason. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/projection.ts:1621]

Exactly five tune rows move under the real embedder and all five already carried a command in the brief: `cmd-doctor-env`, `cmd-doctor-git`, `cmd-doctor-symlink`, `cmd-speckit-handoff` and `cmd-speckit-plan` each go from `top1: false` to `top1: true` with no loss. The gain is top-1 exactness on rows that already offer a command, not reach. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/real-embed-capture.json]

Keeping vectors in step is incremental by construction. Skill refresh compares the stored `vec_content_hash` and `vec_model_id` and skips a row whose text and model are unchanged; only an edited description or a changed model causes an embedding call. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts:1413]

None of the 17 no-command rows gains a command from re-embedding. Five of them already have the expected owner inside the top three, and each is blocked by a non-semantic cause (duplicate suppression, a needs-mode defer, or a mode with no command); the other twelve have the owner absent from the top three or no recommendation at all. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/tune-live.jsonl]

That 28 is the same total iteration 1 measured at the brief (27 head commands plus 1 `Also:` line), so the live measurement regime is the real-embedding regime and the committed fixture baseline's 23 is a regime gap, not a regression. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/tune-live.jsonl]

The measured cost is small at this corpus size: 60 vectors (14 skill + 46 command) at 768 dimensions in a 561 KB SQLite file. `measure-embedder-cost.mjs` reads a warm median of 5.95 ms and p95 of 8.97 ms per embed with the model resident (runner RSS 265,792 KB); re-embedding all 14 skill descriptions is about 83 ms and all 60 vectors about 357 ms, before loop overhead. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/embedder-cost.json]

The real semantic lane embeds less text than the fixture lane. The stored skill vector is the `SKILL.md` frontmatter description alone, while the fixture vector is composed from the skill's name, description, domains, `intentSignals` and `derivedTriggers`, so intent signals reach the cosine lane only under the fixture regime. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/skill-graph/skill-graph-db.ts:737] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/scorer/lanes/semantic-shadow.ts:258]

The real-embedding capture reads plain tune combined 28 of 45 (own 13, attached 15) and holdout 3 of 44, against the committed fixture capture's 23 and 1. Typed stays 44 of 44 (24 own, 20 attached) and false offers stay 0 of 35. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/real-embed-capture.json]

Verdict for rank 15: the measured brief-level gain of enrichment and re-embedding is zero commands on the tune split, because the five rows the vector change moves already offer their command. The floor risk is real but bounded: the real-embedding regime itself holds 0 of 35 false offers and typed 44 of 44, yet rewriting all 14 embedded texts reranks every skill globally and cannot be measured without writing the vectors. Rank 15 stays declined. [INFERENCE: based on findings 1 to 8]

`degradedRecommendations` deliberately collapses every row whose bare slash command does not appear in the prompt into its owner skill, dropping `command`, `policy` and `needsMode`. Plain offers, the doctor hand-off and the needs-mode label are therefore lost by construction on this path, not by accident. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts:1487]

Cold start is no longer a fallback trigger: the hook passes `--no-warm-only`, so the CLI starts the daemon itself and bounds the wait instead of refusing a cold session. What remains is a crashed or unreachable daemon, and a socket-path failure: a `SPECKIT_IPC_SOCKET_DIR` long enough to exceed Darwin's `sun_path` limit makes the CLI exit 69 with a socket-path error and no brief at all. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/skill-advisor-cli-fallback.ts:258]

How often, as recorded: zero realised fallback answers in the measured arms. The 008 cold-start measurement recorded fail-open 0 of 5 with a cold first prompt at 611-844 ms, and the 011 hook health recorded `rollingFailOpenRate` 0 over 3 debug invocations. The only realised hits are deliberate socket sandboxes: the 012 note and the probe above. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/011-typed-command-delivery-and-guards/scratch/hook-health.json]

Measured at HEAD on the plain readme tune prompt: the live daemon answers `sk-doc` with `/create:readme (start)`; the unreachable endpoint answers `system-spec-kit` with no command in 644 ms. That reproduces the 012 note (`write a readme for the utils folder` went to `system-spec-kit` with no command) on the current build. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/degraded-readme.json]

Projected gain and cost: on the tune split the degraded brief would carry 27 head commands plus 1 `Also:` line out of 45, where it carries a command only for a typed prompt today; the plain readme prompt becomes `sk-doc → /create:readme (start)` and the doctor prompt keeps `/doctor:agents-md check (run)`. The measured cost of the Python spawn today is 644 ms for one prompt, so an in-process scorer is not slower. The floors are untouched because the daemon path does not change. [INFERENCE: based on findings 3 and 9]

The hook reader already forwards `command`, `policy`, `needsMode` and `ownerSkillId` when the answer carries them, and maps a `degraded` or `local-scorer` envelope to freshness `stale`. The loss is upstream of the reader, in what the CLI emits. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/hooks/lib/skill-advisor-cli-fallback.ts:382]

The smallest change that carries the same command: in `runLocalScorer`, score in process with the TypeScript fusion scorer and apply the same `enrichCompiledRoutes` step the handler applies, instead of spawning `skill_advisor.py`; keep the Python spawn as the fallback when the built scorer is absent, and keep `degradedRecommendations` as the last resort. This reuses the exact code the daemon runs, so the degraded answer becomes the live answer with freshness `stale`. [INFERENCE: based on findings 1, 2 and 4]

The unreachable-daemon answer is produced by the checked-in Python scorer, not the TypeScript scorer the daemon runs. `runLocalScorer` spawns `skill_advisor.py` with `FORCE_LOCAL=1` and the CLI's own 0.8/0.35 thresholds, then maps the rows for the brief. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/skill-advisor-cli.ts:1453] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/subprocess.ts:294]

There is no persistent counter for this path. The only counter is `hookHealth.rollingFailOpenRate`, which the hook writes only when `SKILL_ADVISOR_DEBUG=1`, so the real frequency outside deliberate sandboxes is UNKNOWN and cannot be quoted from a committed artifact. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/011-typed-command-delivery-and-guards/scratch/hook-health.json]

Which runtimes reach it: every runtime whose hook runs the CLI fallback (Claude, Pi, Devin and DSH in the measured arms). Codex does not reach it at all, because its hooks are unapproved on this checkout: the 013 arm answered delivery `false` on 24 of 24 Codex lines and the delivery leg reads DEGRADED, so Codex gets no brief rather than a degraded one. OpenCode delivery stays `unknown`, so whether its plugin path degrades is unmeasured. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/013-attribution-and-install-reach/implementation-summary.md:117]

`cmd-create-readme-plain-tune-01` routes to `sk-create-quality-control` because its wording names a "quality bar", while `create-readme-aliases` holds `readme`, `write readme`, `folder readme`, `front-page overview` and not `overview page`; the prompt asks for an overview page per folder. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:240] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/command-prompts.jsonl]

`cmd-create-with-human-voice-plain-tune-01` routes to `sk-create-quality-control` from its rewrite-and-score wording; `sk-create-with-human-voice` already declares a `create-with-human-voice-aliases` class that none of this prompt's wording reaches. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:160] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/sk-doc/hub-router.json:163]

Candidate 2 is the only one that can move more than two rows, and it is also the only one whose gain depends on new scoring evidence rather than an alias: five of its six commands already have a scorer row, so the work is anchor wording plus the 35-row silence re-measurement, not new plumbing. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/command-attach.ts:189]

Not recommended, with the reason: rank 15 intent enrichment and re-embedding (iteration 2: 0 brief-level commands gained, and the real regime already holds the floors); the capture `offered` relabel (already built in phase 013 as a comment and field documentation, so re-recommending it would repeat a built item); a lower meaning threshold or a higher semantic lane weight (eliminated in segment two section 4, and iteration 1 shows the no-command rows are not threshold-shaped); a default command for a deferring hub (eliminated in segment two because it fires the deep-loop near-miss row). [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/research-segment-2.md:56]
Ranked candidates, by expected gain in started-when-useful per unit of floor risk:

Residual not covered by the built phase 012 label: `routeNeedsMode` returns true only for a hub with a `MODE_COMMANDS` row, and `sk-code` has none, so `cmd-speckit-implement-plain-tune-01` and `cmd-doctor-sk-code-plain-tune-01` stay silent. This is a gap in the delivered label, not a repeat of rank 6, which built the label for hubs the table already knew. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/lib/command-attach.ts:392]

The alias wording is floor-safe to add: across the 87 `none` rows, the only rows matching `overview|readme|rewrite|human|person wrote|quality bar` are the two typed rows for these same commands, which must start. No must-not-start, near-miss or partial-slash row can be reached by the proposed keywords. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/command-prompts.jsonl]

Candidate 1's full exposure is measured: 0 of 35 floor rows, 0 of the other 52 `none` rows, and at most 1 other tune row if the wrong keyword is chosen. That makes it the lowest-risk change that moves a row. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/none-floor-live.jsonl]

Candidate 1's human-voice wording must avoid the bare word `rewrite`. `cmd-create-diff-plain-tune-01` already carries `/create:diff` and its prompt is a before-and-after rewrite request, so a bare `rewrite` keyword would steal a working row; the exact phrases `reads like a person` and `score how human` appear only on the human-voice row. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/command-prompts.jsonl]

Candidate 1's readme keyword is isolated: `overview page` appears only on `cmd-create-readme-plain-tune-01`, so adding it cannot move another tune row. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/command-prompts.jsonl]

The doctor-family risk set for candidate 2 is exactly three rows: `mns-chat-03` (must-not-start, top score 0.090611), `nm-system-skilled-doctor-01` (near-miss, 0.240312) and `sv-03` (partial slash, 0.125331). They are the only silent rows a doctor anchor can reach, and their top scores are 0.09 to 0.24. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/none-floor-live.jsonl]

The floor baseline at HEAD is clean: 0 of 35 silent rows carry a command, 15 return no recommendation at all, and 20 return a skill-only head. Any offer on these rows is a floor break, so candidate 2 has no slack. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/none-floor-live.jsonl]

The narrow band for candidate 2 is therefore between a new anchor strong enough to pass the 0.8 confidence gate on the five below-threshold rows and weak enough to stay under three doctor-top rows scoring 0.09 to 0.24. That band is the reason it ranks below a two-row alias despite moving more rows. [INFERENCE: based on findings 1 and 2]

The three doctor-top floor rows pass the render gate on confidence 0.82 and uncertainty 0.22 to 0.34 while scoring 0.09 to 0.24, so the floor is protected by the ranking band, not by a comfortable score margin; candidate 2's verification must name those three row ids, not only the aggregate 0 of 35. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/none-floor-live.jsonl]

Every one of the 17 no-command rows maps to a candidate: 1 to the duplicate-suppression fix, 2 to the sk-doc alias fix, 2 to the silent-hub label fix, 6 to the below-threshold anchors, and 2 to the wrong-top doctor fix; the remaining 4 already print `(needs a mode)` and are an intentional ask, not a defect. [INFERENCE: based on iterations 1 and 4]

Final ranking by expected gain in started-when-useful per unit of risk: (1) sk-doc readme and human-voice aliases, +2 rows, zero floor exposure; (2) below-threshold anchors plus one scorer row, up to +6 rows, the only candidate with real floor risk; (3) the silent-hub label for `sk-code`, +2 actionable labels; (4) in-process TypeScript scoring on the degraded path, 28 rendered commands instead of 0 on untyped rows whenever the daemon is down; (5) the duplicate-suppression fix, +1 row; (6) the doctor wrong-top pair, +2 rows, medium-high risk. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/iterations/iteration-004.md]

Of the 28 rendered commands, 22 are the exact corpus label and 6 are a documented subcommand (`/doctor:agents-md check`, `/doctor:ci report`, `/doctor:env list`, `/doctor:git hooks`, `/doctor:overlay status`, `/doctor:symlink link`). Exact-string metrics therefore understate plain reach by 6 rows at HEAD, and that is a corpus-label decision for the operator, not a routing defect. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/tune-live.jsonl]

The four numbers describe one state under four definitions: the committed fixture capture's 23 is expected-command reach through bridge row ids under fixture vectors; the real-embedding capture's 28 is the same metric under the operator's vectors; the live brief renders 27 head commands plus 1 `Also:` line, which is 28 rows carrying a command; and candidate 1 projects 30. None of them is a regression of another. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/real-embed-capture.json]

The lane's three questions are answered with commands and file evidence: (a) 17 rows and six causes, each named by row id; (b) re-embedding and intent enrichment declined again, measured at 0 brief-level commands and priced at about 83 ms for all 14 skill vectors with hash-gated incremental refresh; (g) the fallback runs the Python scorer and then collapses untyped rows, measured at 644 ms and 0 observed occurrences in the recorded arms. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/009-ux-performance-cross-cli-research/research/lineages/offer-reach-3/prompts/degraded-readme.json]

Three gaps remain, all measurement rather than routing: no persistent counter records how often the local-scorer fallback answers; OpenCode's degraded behaviour is unmeasured because its delivery is `unknown`; and the six subcommand labels need an operator decision on whether the corpus should name the subcommand. [SOURCE: specs/system-skill-advisor/routing-and-scoring/008-command-surfacing-build/011-typed-command-delivery-and-guards/scratch/hook-health.json]

Verification per candidate is already executable with committed scripts: `compiled-route.cjs --hub sk-doc --prompt` for the alias modes; `capture-command-routing-baseline.mjs --real-embedding` (no `--write`) for the tune and false-offer lines; the advisor suite for the label and duplicate changes; a new unreachable-endpoint vitest for the degraded path; and the three named floor row ids (`mns-chat-03`, `nm-system-skilled-doctor-01`, `sv-03`) for the anchor work. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-skill-advisor/runtime/scripts/routing-accuracy/capture-command-routing-baseline.mjs:36]

ruledOutDirections.text: `cmd-create-skill-parent-plain-tune-01`: no scorer row and no hub route, so no command can attach without new evidence; it is an alias or scorer-row question, not a table edit.
`cmd-doctor-skill-advisor-plain-tune-01`: the command has seven subcommands and no default, so no single command can be attached without a policy decision about which subcommand a bare request means.
Counting the whole top three as "offered". The renderer emits one head plus an optional doctor `Also:` line, so a rank-2 command is invisible in 16 of the 17 no-command rows.

Reading the committed `attachedMetrics.plain.tune` line as a brief-offer count. It measures expected-command reach through scorer row ids and hub attach at capture time; the live head disagrees on six rows, so it cannot enumerate the rows this iteration asks about.
